title: GoldenWeb Design system
subtitle: A guide to creating consistent, user-centric experiences
thumbnailDescription: A guide to creating consistent, user-centric experiences.

sections.heading: About the project
sections.role: UI, UX, interaction design, and testing

sections.heading: The goal
sections.overviewBody:
Streamline the user experience, ensure brand consistency, and accelerate development while maintaining a user-centered approach. The GoldenWeb Design System, is a guide to creating consistent, user-centric, and straightforward experiences across the product.
At the core, this are our main goals:

items.title: Unify experience
items.description: Create a cohesive and consistent user experience across the entire product.

items.title: Consistency
items.description: Provide a set of standardized design components, patterns, and guidelines that ensure a cohesive and recognizable look and feel throughout our products.

items.title: Scalability
items.description: Design a system that can accommodate future growth and expansion while maintaining visual and functional harmony.

items.title: Collaboration
items.description: Facilitate collaboration between design, development, and other teams by establishing a shared design language.

items.title: Efficiency
items.description: Increase design and development efficiency and speed by providing a centralized resource for UI components, patterns, and guidelines.

items.title: Accesibility
items.description: Prioritize inclusive design principles to ensure the product is usable and enjoyable.

items.title: Desktop & Touch Screen
items.description: Multiapoyo's Pawnshop OS is a web-based platform, so this design system is intended for desktop web usage, but considered to be used on a touch screen too.

sections.heading: The solution V1
sections.description: This was the first version of the GoldenWeb Design system

typography.description: We selected Work Sans because it works the best for web and it's available on Google fonts.

colors.description: We selected a green color for the main one, because we carried it from the legacy of the existing software on the company.

gridsCard.title: Grids and layouts
gridsCard.description: The software is intended for low resolution desktop browser, so the main frame is 1280x832 and mobile is 360x800 because our target user uses mainly android phones with large screens.

iconographyCard.title: Iconography
iconographyCard.description: We selected the Material design symbols library from Google because it was more time efficient for the design team and development team at the time.

sections.heading: The solution V2
sections.description: After the MVP was released, management brought along a brand design team, so we had to adapt our Design system to accommodate the new brand design.

typography.description: The rebranding of the product included a second typeface, which we used only for heading and subtitles.

colors.description: The rebranding introduced a completely new color palette, much more vibrant, but we adjusted it for accessibility.

gridsCard.title: Grids and layouts
gridsCard.description: The software is intended for low resolution desktop browser, so the main frame is 1280x832 and mobile is 360x800 because our target user uses mainly android phones with large screens.

iconographyCard.title: Iconography
iconographyCard.description: We selected the Material design symbols library from Google for design and development efficiency.

sections.heading: Visual design
sections.description: Some instances of the new and current design system in use

cards.title: Atoms
cards.description: Foundational color tokens (#5A5AFF, #2A2C2F, #FFFFFF), typography scales (Tragic Grotesk & Work Sans), and Material Design action icons.

cards.title: Molecules
cards.description: Interactive form fields with filter selects, help tooltips, and primary action buttons with directional chevrons.

cards.title: Organisms
cards.description: Multi-field form groups combining labeled select inputs, required text fields, and validation states.

cards.title: Templates
cards.description: Complete information-input modal dialogs with structured headers, grouped form sections, and Cancelar / Acción principal actions.

items.description: We tested the integration of the first version of the design system on the development of the MVP and created a repository of components.
We tested the accessibility of the typography, colors and icons.
We tested the interactions and micro interactions at the same time as we tested the design prototype.

items.title: Development acceleration
items.description: According to management and front development leaders, the design system accelerated the creation of the MVP about 20%. And for the design team, we were able to ensure all the designs across the product were consistent and unified.

items.title: First version was too small
items.description: On the testing of the first version, users struggled to read some of the text, specially on descriptions.We increased the size of the typographies across the board fot the second versión.

cards.title: Challenges along the way
cards.description:
After the MVP was released, management brought along a brand design team, so we had to adapt our Design system to accommodate the new brand design.
We planned ahead by creating a design system with powerful variants and properties that allowed us to change and redesign with ease.

cards.title: What I would do differently
cards.description:
I would have ensured that the whole design team and future members were aligned on terms of how to document and create components, variants and properties.
I would have used a color palette that better suited web design and accessibility parameters, instead of aligning with the brand design that was intended for publicity.
